title: Lieferung, Implementierung, Migration und Betrieb einer technischen Überwachungstechnologie zur Absicherung der Passagierausgänge A & B im Terminal 1 (Gegenlaufdetektionssystem - GDS)
description: Nach § 8 LuftSiG gehört die Überwachung der Ausgänge aus dem Sicherheitsbereich der Terminals zu der Aufgabe des Flughafenbetreibers. Diese werden aktuell personell überwacht. Hierbei stellt das Sicherheitspersonal sicher, dass keine Menschen oder Gegenstände aus dem unkontrollierten Bereich des Terminals über die Ausgänge in den Sicherheitsbereich gelangen. Sobald sich ein Mensch in den Passagierausgang in Richtung Sicherheitsbereich bewegt, hat das eingesetzte Sicherheitspersonal die Aufgabe, den Menschen über das Fehlverhalten zu informieren und sofern notwendig sich in den Weg zu stellen. Eine mögliche Vermischung von bereits kontrollierten Passagieren und unkontrollierten Personen kann zu einer Räumung des betroffenen Bereichs führen. Die Überwachung des betroffenen Bereichs der Passagierausgänge erfolgt aktuell durch eingesetztes ein dort rund um die Uhr sitzendes Sicherheitspersonal. Durch den Einsatz einer technischen Lösung sollen die bisherigen Aufgaben des Sicherheitspersonals zur Überwachung der Passagierausgänge abgelöst werden. Zur Realisierung der Lösung werden optische Sensoren (bspw. LiDar-Sensoren oder Kameras) präferiert, die durch das Erfassen von Personen und das Überschreiten von definierten Alarmzonen einen Alarm auslösen. Zusätzlich zur Überwachung der Passagiere werden für die Realisierung der Maßnahmen je Alarmstufe zusätzliche Technologien, wie Projektoren, Lautsprecher, Blitzleuchten und Relais-Schaltung für das Verschließen von Türen eingesetzt. Ebenso ist das System an bestehende Alarmierungssysteme der Fraport AG anzubinden, sodass eine Alarmauslösung in den entsprechenden Leitstellen signalisiert wird. Während des Vergabeverfahrens wird mit den wirtschaftlichsten 2 Bietern eine Teststellung (PoC) durchgeführt. Mit dem Teilnahmeantrag ist die von Fraport bereitgestellte Vertraulichkeitsvereinbarung unterzeichnet einzureichen.

title: CONCEPT OF A NEXT GENERATION MCC - EXPRO+
description: The main objective of this activity is to comprehensively gather, analyse and consolidate the requirements and specifications for afuture concept of a Measurement Command Control (MCC) system intended to support ESA propulsion test facilities[ID2.1][ID2.2][ID2.3] for systems and subsystems in a five- to ten-year timeframe. The main use case of such an MCC will be for larger test bench facilities such as the P5 at DLR Lampoldshausen and PF50 at Vernon (hundreds of simultaneous measurements within a large frequency spectrum) but shall be highly adaptable to other similar benches. The activity shall identify innovative technologies, architectural concepts, to support the following objectives:Improve Operational efficiency, maintainability, scalability and performance;SupportStandardization;Ensure energy efficiency for Sustainability purposesReduce Recurring Costs.Subsequently, the study aims to formulate a comprehensive concept for the future MCC, including preliminary system requirements, architectural definition, innovativefeatures, and an assessment of existing and emerging solutions and suppliers ideally from ESA Member States. Thus, the study shall assess the availability and maturity of the required technologies within the European ecosystem, identify potential capability gaps,and recommend developments needed to strengthen European technological autonomy, resilience, and sovereignty in this strategic domain. The resulting concept shall establish the foundations for future procurement and implementation activities across ESA propulsiontest facilities.[ID3.1][ID3.2][ID3.3] Particular attention shall be given to disruptive concepts and architectural evolutions capable of delivering a substantial leap in the bench capabilities with respect to the given objectives.

title: RAYLEIGH GUIDE STAR FOR ADAPTIVE OPTICS IN OPTICAL COMMUNICATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.075) EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to evaluate the use of a Rayleigh guide star as a reference beacon for adaptive opticspre-and post-compensation for optical communication through the atmosphere.Targeted Improvements:75% reduction in cost and complexity with respect to the use of a Sodium guide star laserDescription:The use of a Rayleigh guide star as a reference beacon for optical pre-and post-compensation over the current Sodium laser solution would allow for a considerable decrease in both the cost and complexity of the laser system required for adaptive optics in optical links through the atmosphere.The Rayleigh guide star shall be evaluated for its suitability and be compared to existing solutions, to demonstrate the potential improvements. An evaluation of the sub-system, the choice of equipment and the operational implementation shall be addressed for use on optical communication links through the atmosphere. The activity will perform a numerical study comparing the main possible beacons to be used as reference for pre- and post-compensation in Adaptive Optics (AO) in the context of optical communications, using as a reference the 3 main solutions: Sodium Guide Star, Beacon from the satellite and Rayleigh Guide Star. A selection of suitable equipment solutions will need to be chosen and the impact of the beacon method on the global architecture/cost, ease of operation/complexity/laser safety of backscattered light evaluated. Upon a positive solution being proposed, integration and tests will be conducted in a laboratory environment, and then on-sky tests will be conducted.

title: END-TO-END MODELLING OF THE RADIATION HARDNESS ASSURANCE PROCESS - EXPRO+
description: Objectives: To develop an integrated software toolkit to assess the relative contributions to overall errors and uncertainties in the radiation hardness assurance process and estimate the true risk of failures. Description: The current process for Radiation Hardness Assurance (RHA) attempts to ensure compliance to mission robustness, reliability and availability with respect to radiation. This includes a range of measures addressed at different stages of the process. environment models are often applied with confidence levels and margins which in isolation may not sufficiently mitigate risk, the transport of radiation through shielding can incorporatea great deal of hidden margin (depending on the level of detail of the radiation model) but this can also be reduced to near-zero through detailed analysis and effects in components based on test data are highly susceptible to component specifics combined with other degradation parameters and temperature variations. Given this myriad of factors the true risk of component failure is not easy to discern. This activity shall address Radiation Hardness Assurance (RHA) as an integrated approach from radiation environment modelling to component acceptance to determine true risk levels for the end-to-end process. This shall include assessment of the probabilities of component failure for various environments using different methods for capturing environmental variability, radiation model fidelity and uncertainties in component test data and related statistical approaches. This shall be able to incorporate a digital representation of the spacecraft for radiation transport, test data for components and a range of orbital environments thereby spanning multiple disciplines in spacecraft design and quality assurance and extracting benefits from adopting a Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) approach. The system shall incorporate estimates of errors and uncertainties at each step of the process to derivean estimate of the true risk of failure. This activity shall encompass the following tasks: - Investigate the requirements and definition of process by consultation with radiation experts in industry as well as at ESA - Establish the use cases and collect relevant radiation effects data to test in the software; - Design of the software architecture leveraging existing assets to link orbits, environments, propagation and effects; - Develop algorithms to propagate uncertainties through the different steps of the RHA process;- Derivation of "true risk" estimates and comparison with current approaches; - Make recommendations for the maturation of this integrated (MBSE) approach Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl.
